stresses: A combustion-safety-only recording (shell was captured on a separate file, explicitly not negated here -- a REDIRECTION, not a rule-4 disclaimer). THE clearest corpus instance of the ambient-vs-undiluted-flue-CO confusability (RECONCILIATION.md ruling 4): 'The furnace flue itself was fine but ambient CO in the room climbed to thirty-five ppm' contrasts a flue-side reading against a room-side reading in one sentence -- the annotators split on this outright, one asserting healthUndilutedFlueCo: Passed, the other leaving it unmentioned on the theory that 'fine' might describe the flue's physical condition rather than a CO reading; resolved per ruling 4 to healthUndilutedFlueCo: Passed because the flue is explicitly named. Six of the 13 health-matrix tests get explicit, distinct verdicts and three MORE are individually named and declared not-in-scope ('Mold, asbestos, lead ... none of that was in scope') -- rule 8's 'name the specific test' pattern, not a blanket disclaimer. The furnace mention reproduces the hvacSystemEquipmentType/shared-ducts schema conflation. A dhwLocation ('the utility room') names a real, specific location without stating its conditioning status, fitting no DhwLocation member cleanly -- noFittingMember, per THE ONE RULE (something was said; omission is not the answer just because the mapping is unclear). The worst-case-depressurization procedure states a pressure reading that sets up the worst-case-spillage verdict, but the auditor never renders a pass/fail/warning verdict for the depressurization test itself as its own leaf -- genuinely unmentioned, not a schema gap.

notes.health.healthUndilutedFlueCo: RULING 4 SITE (see RECONCILIATION.md): 'The furnace flue itself was fine but ambient CO in the room climbed to thirty-five ppm' explicitly names the flue in direct contrast with the room/ambient reading in the same breath -- the corpus's clearest textual instance of the ambient-CO-vs-undiluted-flue-CO confusability the schema does not disambiguate on its own. Applying the reconciliation rule (undiluted flue CO only when the flue/a probe/combustion gas is explicitly named), this resolves to Passed. One annotator on this transcript left the leaf unmentioned, reading 'fine' as possibly describing the flue's physical/mechanical condition rather than a CO measurement; the ruling is applied uniformly here in favor of asserting it, given the explicit 'flue' word and the sentence's own 'but' contrast against the ambient figure.
notes.dhw.dhwType2: 'Storage water heater' is the standard industry term for a tank-type unit (as opposed to tankless/on-demand); it maps to 'Tank Water Heater' with no other DhwType member fitting instead.
notes._general: health.healthWorstCaseDepressurization is left unmentioned -- the auditor narrates the depressurization procedure and a pressure reading ('minus fifty pascals') that sets up the worst-case-spillage test, but never states a pass/fail/warning verdict for the depressurization test itself as its own leaf, only for spillage; converting the raw pressure into a verdict would be exactly the derivation rule 3 forbids. hvac.hvacUpgradeAction is left unmentioned -- 'I shut the furnace down' is an immediate safety shutdown taken during testing, not one of the four upgrade-action members, so it is not parked there. The opening line ('I did the shell separately on another file') is NOT treated as a disclaimer -- it confirms the shell WAS captured, just in a different recording, so no shell-related leaf or namedSet is negated by it; those leaves are simply, correctly unmentioned by default for THIS transcript. health.healthRadon, health.healthElectrical, health.healthRoofCondition, and every basedata/attic/wall/window leaf are never mentioned at all in this combustion-only transcript.
